title: Doctors Raise Fresh Questions About Trump Health as He Turns 80
excerpt: Persistent bruising, leg swelling, and apparent drowsiness during public events have prompted multiple physicians — including Dick Cheneys former cardiologist — to call for greater transparency about the presidents medical condition.
body:
• President Trump, who turned 80 in June 2026, has faced recurring scrutiny over visible bruising on his hands, swollen legs, and episodes of apparent drowsiness during public events.
  • Dr. Jonathan Reiner, cardiologist to the late Vice President Dick Cheney, has repeatedly questioned the White House's medical disclosures and called for a congressional inquiry into presidential fitness.
  • Trump was diagnosed with chronic venous insufficiency in July 2025, and his White House physician says he remains in excellent health.
  • Medical disclosures from the White House have grown less detailed over the course of Trumps second term, with his latest health readout released late on a Friday night three days after the checkup.

Visible Signs Draw Medical Scrutiny

President Donald Trump has faced a steady drumbeat of health questions since the start of his second term, driven by visible bruising on his hands, swelling in his legs, and multiple instances of appearing to doze off during public events in the White House.

https://x.com/OutFrontCNN/status/2087702295622590894

Trump, who turned 80 in June, is the oldest person to serve as president. His White House physician, Dr. Sean Barbabella, has consistently concluded that Trump remains in excellent health and is fully fit to carry out his duties. But outside medical experts say the White House's disclosures leave significant gaps.

The president has long had bruising on his right hand, which drew increased attention after he began covering it with makeup and bandages. In a January interview with The Wall Street Journal, Trump blamed the bruising on his daily aspirin regimen — 325 milligrams, well above the standard 81-milligram dose his doctors recommend.

"They say aspirin is good for thinning out the blood, and I dont want thick blood pouring through my heart. I want nice, thin blood pouring through my heart."

— President Donald Trump, Wall Street Journal interview

Cheneys Former Cardiologist Weighs In

Dr. Jonathan Reiner, a cardiologist at George Washington University who served as the late Vice President Dick Cheneys heart doctor, has been one of the most prominent medical voices questioning Trumps health disclosures.

After the White House released a three-page health readout from Trumps May 2026 visit to Walter Reed National Military Medical Center — released at 10:44 PM on a Friday night, three days after the checkup — Reiner wrote on X that the report left critical questions unanswered.

He questioned why Trump has undergone repeated CT scans of his heart during checkups and whether the medical team addressed his daytime fatigue and sleepiness. Reiner also dismissed Trumps aspirin explanation as medical nonsense.

"That makes no sense. That actually makes nonsense," Reiner told CNN. "When we use any kind of anticoagulant medications to prevent clotting, those dont thin the blood. Particularly for people over the age of 70, not only is there no benefit in terms of primary prevention, there can be hazard."

Chronic Venous Insufficiency Diagnosis

In July 2025, the White House disclosed that Trump had been diagnosed with chronic venous insufficiency — a condition where veins in the lower legs have difficulty returning blood to the heart, leading to swelling. The condition is common in people over 70 and is not considered life-threatening.

However, some outside physicians have been skeptical of this explanation. Dr. Daniel J. Rader, a cardiologist at the University of Pennsylvania, told The New York Times that venous insufficiency "almost never" causes swelling in both ankles, as was observed with Trump.

The May 2026 readout noted that Trumps lower leg swelling had improved from the previous year and put his weight at 238 pounds — 14 pounds more than his April 2025 physical. An AI-enhanced electrocardiogram estimated his cardiac age at approximately 14 years younger than his chronological age, a finding some clinicians questioned as not standard diagnostic practice.

Declining Transparency

Medical disclosures from the White House have grown progressively less detailed over the course of Trumps second term. His April 2025 physical produced a three-page report including bloodwork and medications. The October 2025 visit yielded a vague memo that was not released until December.

Dr. Bob Wachter, chair of the Department of Medicine at the University of California, San Francisco, noted that the frequency of Trumps checkups — four publicly acknowledged visits in his second term — was itself unusual.

"I think its quite unusual for someone who doesnt have chronic problems that require more frequent monitoring to come in more often than every year," Wachter said.

By May 2026, multiple polls showed a majority of Americans did not believe Trump was mentally fit to serve as president. Trump has dismissed all health concerns, posting on Truth Social that he has "aced" cognitive tests and is in "PERFECT HEALTH."
